name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network and dirt ground, seen as a flat top-down terrain tileset

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain tile sheet: dark asphalt road pieces (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, a large filled block) sit on a brown dirt ground. The sheet is 256 px wide and 192 rows tall, fully opaque. It is viewed straight from above, and no south-facing vertical face, eave line or standing volume is drawn. The column scans show only repeating horizontal texture bands (dirt and asphalt patches, cracks, an oil stain), not a front face. For terrain this is the expected flat ground, but by the measurement rules it has no front face of 3 or more rows, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference. Its 5 visible tones per tile sit between the grass (3) and the paving (7), and near-flat coverage is 3%, so the surface is not flat. The dirt has a mottled grain of about 4 browns, which reads acceptably. The asphalt is the weak part: it is a blue-grey with about 3-4 steps and only a faint speckle. The cracks, repair patch and oil stain are barely readable; the patch is just a slightly different speckle at the right. The road edges are clean blocky rectangles, with no darker broken lip, loose chunks or crumbling, so the described edge treatment is missing. There is no real outline, only value separation, and the dark edge pixels carry a tint (0% neutral), so it is not a sticker look. Shading depth and texture detail are still below the Beodeul references, which have about 5-6 steps per material and per-stone or per-tuft detail.

surfaces.part: asphalt road network tiles on dirt ground (flat ground autotile sheet)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain autotile sheet seen straight down: a full-width 256px opaque dirt field with dark asphalt road pieces (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, a large filled block). The column scan shows repeating texture bands with no front-edge line, eave shadow or vertical face. The road is a flat ground surface and has no standing front face, so it is a top-down ground texture as expected for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total, split between the asphalt and the dirt, so each material gets about 4 lightness steps against roughly 6 on the paving reference. The asphalt reads as a mottled blue-grey with speckle. The long hairline cracks, the oil stain and the darker broken lip along the crumbling edges are barely visible at this scale. The repair patch shows only as faint marks in the right-hand block. The dirt is a repeated 3-4 tone noise with no clear soil grain or loose chunks. Measured facts are mixed. The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for paving and 3 for grass, near-flat coverage is 3%, and its dark edge pixels carry a tint (0% neutral), so it is not a black sticker outline. Even so, the asphalt is plain mottling and does not match the reference's per-element shading, and the requested details are missing or too faint. When in doubt, fail.
